definitions.gloss: two nights (of lodging); a two-night stay
definitions.explanation: Two nights spent away from home in paid or borrowed accommodation. Japanese counts trips by nights rather than days, so a stay is booked and described in {泊|はく} first and days second.

examples.japanese: {二泊|にはく}{予約|よやく}しました。
{京都|きょうと}に{二泊三日|にはくみっか}で{行|い}く{予定|よてい}です。
examples.english: I'm planning a three-day, two-night trip to Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {一泊|いっぱく}のつもりだったが、{楽|たの}しくて{二泊|にはく}に{延|の}ばした。
examples.english: I had meant to stay one night, but I was enjoying it so much that I stretched it to two.

examples.japanese: {出張|しゅっちょう}は{二泊|にはく}なので、{荷物|にもつ}は{機内持|きないも}ち{込|こ}みで{足|た}ります。
examples.english: The business trip is two nights, so carry-on luggage will be enough.

notes:
The counter {泊|はく} counts nights of lodging. Watch the sound changes: {一泊|いっぱく}, {二泊|にはく}, {三泊|さんぱく}, {四泊|よんはく}, {六泊|ろっぱく}, {八泊|はっぱく}, {十泊|じっぱく}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {二泊三日|にはくみっか}: three days and two nights
- {二泊|にはく}する: to stay two nights
- {二泊分|にはくぶん}の{料金|りょうきん}: the charge for two nights

USAGE:
Trip lengths are stated nights-first as {一泊二日|いっぱくふつか}, {二泊三日|にはくみっか}, {三泊四日|さんぱくよっか} — the reverse of the English order, and the form used in tour names and travel plans.
